os-addr-translation.caption: Dynamic relocation: the MMU adds the relocation register (14000) to every logical address (346) to get the physical address (14346).

os-paging-model.caption: Paging in one picture: a process is cut into equal pages, memory into equal frames, and any page can sit in any free frame.

os-paging-hw.caption: Paging hardware: the page number *p* indexes the page table to get frame *f*; the offset *d* is copied as-is.

os-paging-example.caption: Paging example: a 16-byte logical memory with 4-byte pages mapped into a 32-byte physical memory through the page table (5, 6, 1, 2).

os-tlb.caption: Paging hardware with a TLB: on a TLB hit the frame number comes straight from the TLB; on a miss the page table is consulted.

os-valid-bit.caption: Valid (v) / invalid (i) bit in the page table: pages 6 and 7 are not part of the process, so touching them traps.

os-page-fault.caption: Steps in handling a page fault: trap → find the page on disk → load it into a free frame → fix the page table → restart the instruction.

os-seg-hw.caption: Segmentation hardware: the segment number picks a (limit, base) pair; the offset must be less than the limit, then base + offset is the physical address.

os-page-replacement.caption: Page replacement: swap out a victim page, mark it invalid, swap in the needed page, reset the page table.

os-swapping.caption: Swapping: a whole process is moved out to secondary memory and another is brought into main memory.

os-disk-fcfs.caption: FCFS disk scheduling for queue 98, 183, 37, 122, 14, 124, 65, 67 with head at 53: total head movement 640 cylinders.

os-disk-sstf.caption: SSTF on the same queue: always serve the nearest request. Total head movement 236 cylinders.

os-disk-scan.caption: SCAN (elevator) moving towards 0 first: the head sweeps to the end, then reverses. Total 236 cylinders.

os-disk-cscan.caption: C-SCAN: sweep one way to the end, jump back to the other end, and continue in the same direction. Total 382 (this figure counts the return jump).

os-disk-clook.caption: C-LOOK: go up only as far as the last request (183), jump back to the lowest pending request (14), and continue upwards.

os-demand-paging.caption: Demand paging: only pages A, C and F are in memory (valid); the rest stay on disk until they are needed.

os-page-table.caption: Free-frame list before (a) and after (b) a new 4-page process is loaded: pages land in frames 14, 13, 18 and 20.

os-many-to-one.caption: Many-to-one model: many user threads share one kernel thread, so one blocking call blocks them all.

os-one-to-one.caption: One-to-one model: every user thread gets its own kernel thread (Linux, Windows).

os-many-to-many.caption: Many-to-many model: many user threads are multiplexed onto a smaller or equal number of kernel threads.

os-bounded-buffer.caption: Bounded buffer: the producer fills slots, the consumer empties them, and the buffer has only *n* slots.

os-rag.caption: A resource allocation graph with no cycle, so no deadlock. Request edges point P → R; assignment edges point R → P.

os-rag-deadlock.caption: Top: a RAG with a cycle and a deadlock. Bottom: a RAG with a cycle but no deadlock, because R1 and R2 have spare instances.

os-safe-state.caption: Safe, unsafe and deadlocked states: deadlock lies inside the unsafe region; staying in safe states guarantees no deadlock.

os-contiguous.caption: Contiguous allocation: each file occupies consecutive blocks; the directory stores the start block and length.

os-linked.caption: Linked allocation: each block holds a pointer to the next block of the file.

os-indexed.caption: Indexed allocation: one index block holds the addresses of all the file's data blocks (file jeep → index block 19).

os-dir-single.caption: Single-level directory: every file of every user sits in one directory.

os-dir-two.caption: Two-level directory: a master file directory points to a separate user file directory for each user.

os-dir-tree.caption: Tree-structured directory: directories can contain subdirectories, giving every file a path.

os-dir-acyclic.caption: Acyclic-graph directory: a file or directory can be shared (linked) from two places, but cycles are not allowed.

os-dir-general.caption: General-graph directory: links may create cycles, so the OS needs garbage collection and cycle-safe traversal.

os-attacks.caption: Masquerade: Darth sends a message that appears to come from Bob. This is one of the standard security attacks.

se-cohesion-types.caption: Cohesion from best to worst: functional, sequential, communicational, procedural, temporal, logical, coincidental.

se-coupling-types.caption: Coupling from best (no direct coupling) to worst (content coupling): data, stamp, control, external, common, content.

se-sc-elements.caption: Structure chart notation: modules as boxes, call lines, data parameters (hollow circle), control flags (filled circle), loops and decisions.

se-sc-example.caption: Structure chart example: Main calls Configure, Process and UpdateReport; Process calls GetInput, CalculateArea and CalculateVolume.

se-arch-data-centred.caption: Data-centred (repository/blackboard) architecture: independent client components share one central data store.

se-arch-data-flow.caption: Data-flow (pipes and filters) architecture: data passes through a series of filters connected by pipes.

se-arch-call-return.caption: Call-and-return (main program/subprogram) architecture: a hierarchy of control from the main program down.

se-arch-layered.caption: Layered architecture: core, utility, application and user-interface layers; each layer serves the one above it.

se-gantt.caption: A Gantt (timeline) chart: each task is a bar on a calendar, so overlaps and dependencies are easy to see.
se-gantt.credit: SE Unit-3 effort estimation slides, slide 15

se-dfd-symbols.caption: DFD symbols: data flow (arrow), process (circle), external entity (rectangle) and data store (open rectangle / parallel lines).

se-dfd-l0-library.caption: Level-0 DFD (context diagram) of a library system: the whole system is one process talking to Student and Librarian.

se-dfd-l0-result.caption: Level-0 DFD of a student result management system with its external entities and outputs.

se-dfd-l1.caption: Level-1 DFD of the library system: the single process splits into 1.0 Issue Book and 2.0 Return Book, with data stores.

se-dfd-l2.caption: Level-2 DFD: process 1.0 Issue Book decomposed into 1.1–1.4.

se-u4-img1.caption: DFD of an ATM system: authenticate customer, process transaction, with account and transaction databases.

se-inspection.caption: Code inspection process: planning → preparation → inspection meeting → rework → follow-up.

se-sa-img21.caption: Incremental development of a student system: each increment adds a feature and re-tests everything built so far.

se-mccall.caption: McCall's quality triangle: product operation (bottom), product revision (left) and product transition (right).

se-t-img9.caption: Sandwich (hybrid) integration: top-down and bottom-up integration run at the same time and meet in the middle.

se-t-img17.caption: The family tree of software testing: manual vs automation, white/black/grey box, functional vs non-functional.

se-t-img19.caption: Levels of testing: unit → integration → system testing on the application code.

se-t-img16.caption: The software testing process as a cycle: set up environment → test cases → test data → execute → report defects → regression → log → retest.

se-risk.caption: Risk management = risk assessment (identify, analyse, prioritise) + risk control (plan, monitor, resolve).
